title: The Kindness of Strangers

beats.what: Boyd surfaces outside the tree and meets Martin, a badly injured man who begs to be killed
Boyd refuses to abandon Martin; the two are trapped as creatures return while they argue
Bus passengers scatter into the night after a man with a gun forces the diner door open; several die outside
Fatima breaks down at the window watching people die outside while Ellis physically holds her back
Martin, delirious, cuts Boyd's wrist and says 'my blood is your blood now' before apparently dying
Victor shares his hidden cache with Tabitha; reveals his mother came here with him before she died
Jim is pulled free from the collapsed basement as dawn breaks; the Cohen family reunites

character_beats.beat: Wants to leave no man behind (states the Marine code explicitly); cannot bring himself to kill Martin as requested, which leaves both of them in greater danger and results in the blood exchange
Wants to run out and save people screaming outside; Ellis keeps pulling her back, and she collapses saying she cannot do this anymore, revealing the cost of survival as passivity
Wants to protect his family; spends the entire night pinned under rubble, helpless, while Julie refuses to abandon him, reversing the parent-protector dynamic

key_lines.line: I need you to kill me.
key_lines.why: Martin's first words to Boyd; frames the episode's central moral question about mercy and obligation

key_lines.line: Leave no man behind. You help me, I help you.
key_lines.why: Boyd cites Marine code to justify refusing to abandon Martin; the ethic that will trap him here

key_lines.line: My blood is your blood now.
key_lines.why: Martin's blood-transfer moment; the line whose consequence carries into Boyd's physical symptoms in later episodes

key_lines.line: Even if you forget, the pictures remember.
key_lines.why: Victor articulates the show's memory-and-documentation theme in its simplest form

open_loops: What did the blood exchange between Martin and Boyd actually do to Boyd, and was it deliberate?
Martin said he came through the tree and things got worse on the other side: what is on the other side of the tree?
Victor's mother died in this place; Victor refers to a boy in white as his friend who went away and came back: who is this boy?
The gun-toting bus passenger forced the door open and people died; how many bus passengers survived the night?
Martin asked 'what if it is all just a dream' before the blood exchange: what did he know about Abby?

payoffs.what: The man calling to Boyd from above the pit in S02E01 is revealed as Martin, and their deal is now in play

contradiction.wants: to get both himself and Martin out alive, invoking leave-no-man-behind
contradiction.does: his refusal to comply with Martin's wish for death prolongs Martin's suffering and leads directly to the blood-contamination moment Boyd cannot control

tone_notes: Runtime 44.9 min, 767 cues, 72.5 words/min, the lowest dialogue density in this block. Two long silences: 328-433s (the diner locked down and waiting, over 100 seconds of music and near-silence) and 1704-1765s (aftermath of deaths outside, another 61-second quiet stretch). Density spikes at minutes 20-21 (165-154, the diner standoff with the gunman) and 34-35 (176, the mob chaos as the door is forced). The repeated phrase 'move move move' (five occurrences) captures the episode's physical urgency. Leonard Cohen's 'Who by Fire' plays over the dawn reunion, the lyrics cataloguing ways to die over images of survival.
